message.reasoning:
We need to decide whether to pay fine or roll for doubles. Current cash 700, fine 50. Rolling for doubles has chance 1/6? Actually probability of doubles is 6/36 = 1/6. If fail, you stay in jail and lose turn, but you can try again next turn? Usually you have up to 3 attempts then must pay. Here we have many cash, fine is cheap. Paying now gets out and can collect rent from properties. We have several properties with houses: Kentucky, Indiana, Illinois each have 3 houses. Those are orange? Actually Kentucky, Indiana, Illinois are red? Wait: Kentucky Avenue is red? Actually Monopoly: Kentucky Avenue is red, Indiana Avenue red, Illinois Avenue red. So we have a monopoly with 3 houses each, good rent. Being in jail prevents us from collecting rent when others land on them? Actually you can still collect rent while in jail. So staying in jail doesn't stop rent collection. But you can't move to land on others' properties to collect? Actually you only collect when others land on yours. So being in jail doesn't affect that. However you miss chance to land on high-rent spaces like Boardwalk etc. But you have cash 700, fine 50 is cheap. Paying fine gets you out and you can move next turn. Rolling for doubles could waste a turn and maybe you could roll again later. Since cash is abundant, paying fine is safe. Also you might want to conserve cash for building houses/hotels later. But 50 is small relative to 700. So pay fine.

Public message: maybe say "I'll pay the fine and get back to business." Could also be strategic: maybe bluff about not paying to keep others guessing? But no benefit. So pay.

Make tool call pay_jail_fine with private_thought and public_message.
